The test image displays a sugarcane leaf with prominent symptoms. The leaf shows variegation, with parallel stripes of green and a pale yellow or white color running along its length. On this discolored, lighter stripe, there is a distinct, elongated, reddish lesion that contains several small, white, pustule-like dots. The affected plant part is clearly the leaf.

First, I will consult the `part_index.md` file to determine which diseases are documented to affect sugarcane leaves. This will narrow down the possibilities from the initial list of nine classes.

The `part_index.md` file confirms that the following classes from my list affect the **leaf**: Brown_Spot, Leaf_Scald, Pokkah_Boeng, Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv, Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus, Yellow_Leaf, and Yellow_Spot. Grassy_Shoot is listed under `whole_plant` and Sett_Rot under `stem`, making them less likely candidates based on the visual evidence of a single diseased leaf.

The test image shows a distinct reddish lesion with white pustules on a yellow/white striped area of the leaf. The "Leaf_Scald" description mentions a "white 'pencil line' on the leaf," which aligns well with the striped pattern. "Pokkah_Boeng" mentions red streaking, which is also a possibility.

I will now start viewing the reference images to compare visually. I will prioritize the most likely candidates based on the combination of the striped leaf pattern and the reddish lesion. My first reference image will be for Leaf_Scald.
